Modified read with SLOOS context:

- Policy stance and tone: The FOMC kept the target range at 4.25–4.50% and continued balance-sheet runoff, emphasizing data dependence. Activity is described as solid with low unemployment; inflation remains somewhat above target. Uncertainty has diminished but is still elevated.

- SLOOS cross-check (April 2025): Banks reported tighter credit supply and softer demand, which temper the growth-positive tone of the statement.
  • Standards/terms: Banks tightened standards for commercial real estate (CRE) lending and tightened terms for C&I loans; other (non-large) banks tightened C&I standards, while large banks’ C&I standards were broadly unchanged; foreign banks tightened C&I terms.
  • Demand: Weaker demand reported for CRE loans (foreign and large banks) and softer customer financing/investment needs; changes to credit lines also reported.
  • Reasons cited: Economic outlook, supervisory actions, legislative/accounting changes, industry-specific problems, and lower risk tolerance.

- Implications for transmission and risks: The combination of restrictive policy (unchanged rate, ongoing QT) and SLOOS-indicated tightening/weak demand points to headwinds for credit availability and investment, especially in CRE and parts of C&I. This supports a cautious, risk-balanced stance and argues against a strong pro-growth read despite solid activity and low unemployment.

Bottom line: The communication remains balanced-to-slightly-hawkish on inflation, but SLOOS-driven credit headwinds and weaker demand restrain the net tone. Overall sentiment is only marginally positive.
